reasoning: S1 is valid, but global retention of half the mass does not imply retention of half the contribution inside a density-maximizing interval. An exact counterexample gives C_F(H)=2 while C_F(G)/2=5/2. S3 would be valid if S2 were established; S4 does not repair the failure.

issue.explanation: The retained intervals may all lie outside an interval realizing D(G), leaving none of its interval-volume contribution.

witness: Let G contain five labeled copies of [0,1/10], together with the five intervals [k/10,(k+1)/10] for k=2,3,4,5,6. Let H consist precisely of those latter five intervals. Every interval has length 1/10 and full shading. The total masses are 1 for G and 1/2 for H. The intervals of H have pairwise disjoint interiors, so the sum of lengths of intervals contained in any J is at most |J|; equality occurs when J is any member of H. Thus D(H)=1. The multiplicity of G is at most five almost everywhere, which implies its contained-interval density is at most five for every J. Taking J=[0,1/10] attains five, so D(G)=5. Consequently C_F(H)=2<5/2=C_F(G)/2. In this maximizing J, H retains zero contribution.
